items.title: CVE-2026-77000 (CRITICAL 9.8): The WP Social Media Login WordPress plugin through 1.0.6 does not verify that a social login was actually com…
items.one_liner: WordPress sites running WP Social Media Login <= 1.0.6 can be completely taken over by unauthenticated attackers.
items.summary: The WP Social Media Login WordPress plugin through version 1.0.6 fails to verify whether a social login was completed with an identity provider before authenticating a visitor. This flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to supply any user's email address, including administrative accounts, and log in directly as that user. The vulnerability carries a critical CVSS score of 9.8 and enables full account takeover across affected WordPress sites.
key_facts: Affected Plugin: WP Social Media Login through 1.0.6
items.bottom_line: Unauthenticated attackers can log in as any WordPress administrator simply by supplying their email address to vulnerable WP Social Media Login installations.

items.one_liner: A critical RCE flaw in the Windows IKE Extension (CVE-2026-33824) is actively exploited, prompting urgent CISA warnings.
items.summary: CISA has warned that a critical remote code execution vulnerability in the Windows Internet Key Exchange (IKE) Service Extensions component, tracked as CVE-2026-33824, is now actively exploited in the wild. The double-free flaw affects all supported Windows 10, Windows 11, and Windows Server versions, allowing unauthenticated attackers to achieve code execution by sending crafted packets via UDP ports 500 or 4500. Microsoft patched the vulnerability during the April 2026 Patch Tuesday updates and advised blocking inbound traffic on affected ports if patches cannot be immediately installed. CISA has ordered federal civilian agencies to remediate the vulnerability under Binding Operational Directive 26-04.

items.title: CVE-2026-75870 (CRITICAL 9.1): Punk versions before 0.18 for Perl allow session cookie forgery via an empty default HMAC key when a session…
items.one_liner: Perl developers using Punk < 0.18 without explicit session secrets face unauthenticated session forgery.
items.summary: Punk versions before 0.18 for Perl permit session cookie forgery because they default to an empty HMAC key when a session declaration lacks a secret. The cookie read and write-back procedures both assign a zero-length HMAC-SHA256 key when no secret option is provided, allowing an attacker with knowledge of the cookie format to mint offline cookies containing arbitrary user identifiers or roles. This misconfiguration operates without runtime warnings or malformed structures, maintaining normal session round-trips while leaving applications vulnerable.
items.bottom_line: Perl applications running Punk versions prior to 0.18 without an explicit session secret generate zero-length HMAC keys, enabling complete session cookie forgery.

items.title: Disrupting supply chain attacks on npm and GitHub Actions
items.one_liner: GitHub strengthens npm and Actions defaults with account lockouts and safer fork checkouts to stop supply chain attacks.
items.summary: GitHub has implemented several product security improvements across npm and GitHub Actions to disrupt common supply chain attack techniques used to spread malware. New preventive measures include placing high-impact npm accounts into a 72-hour read-only mode when email addresses or 2FA recovery codes are changed. For GitHub Actions, GitHub changed the default behavior of actions/checkout to prevent checking out untrusted code from forks during vulnerable triggers, and introduced granular workflow execution policies for enterprises and organizations. These combined technical constraints and policy controls are designed to break initial compromise vectors often leveraged in malicious open-source campaigns.

items.bottom_line: New default controls on npm and GitHub Actions significantly restrict account takeover and untrusted fork code execution.

items.title: Two CVSS 9.8 Auth Bypasses in miniOrange SAML WordPress Plugin Were Exploited Before Any Database Even Listed the Paid Editions as Vulnerable
items.one_liner: miniOrange SAML WordPress plugin hit by two active CVSS 9.8 auth bypasses that bypassed scanners due to slug versioning confusion.
items.summary: Two critical CVSS 9.8 authentication bypass vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-61979 and CVE-2026-15981, affect the miniOrange SAML 2.0 Single Sign On WordPress plugin and are actively exploited in the wild. CVE-2026-61979 involves an algorithm confusion flaw where the plugin trusts incoming SAML assertions to set HMAC-SHA1 and uses the IdP's public key as a secret, while CVE-2026-15981 relies on PHP's openssl_verify returning -1 on error, which evaluates as true. Because the plugin bundles seven distinct product editions under a single WordPress slug with independent version numbering, automated vulnerability databases and scanners misreported paid installations as patched while they remained vulnerable.
items.bottom_line: Paid editions of the miniOrange SAML WordPress plugin remained vulnerable to active CVSS 9.8 auth bypasses because scanners misread their version numbers as patched.

items.title: Two unvaccinated people die of measles in Pennsylvania
items.one_liner: Surging U.S. measles outbreaks and two deaths in Pennsylvania underscore the real-world dangers of vaccine hesitancy and shifting federal immunization policies.
items.summary: Two unvaccinated individuals have died of measles in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, where only 85% of kindergarten-age students are vaccinated—well below the 95% herd immunity threshold. The state has recorded 393 cases this year, contributing to a national total of 2,777 confirmed measles cases across the U.S. in the first seven months of 2026. The rising infection numbers coincide with increasing vaccine hesitancy and recent federal policy actions, including an executive order from President Donald Trump calling for fewer childhood vaccinations and splitting the MMR vaccine. Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro criticized federal rhetoric and health secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. for propagating vaccine misinformation.

items.title: Unpatched Zimbra servers are falling to CVE-2026-73570 attacks
items.one_liner: An unauthenticated remote code execution flaw in Zimbra servers is actively exploited in the wild, requiring immediate patching.
items.summary: At least 274 internet-facing Zimbra Collaboration Suite servers have been compromised by unknown attackers exploiting CVE-2026-73570, a code injection flaw in versions prior to v10.1.20. The vulnerability occurs when the optional zimbra-snmp package is installed and SNMP notifications are enabled, allowing unauthenticated attackers to send crafted SMTP requests that execute arbitrary OS commands. Shadowserver noted that over 8,200 instances remain unpatched, though not all may have the vulnerable configuration exposed.

items.title: ZDI-26-609: Linux Kernel Net Scheduler Packet Classifier Use-After-Free Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability
items.one_liner: Linux kernel net scheduler flaw in route4_set_fastmap permits local attackers to achieve root code execution.
items.summary: A use-after-free vulnerability exists within the route4_set_fastmap function of the Linux Kernel Net Scheduler packet classifier. The flaw stems from a lack of validation regarding an object's existence prior to performing operations on it. Local attackers who obtain low-privileged code execution capabilities can exploit this vulnerability to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary code in the context of the kernel. Linux has released a patch via upstream commit 47d7f7051253bdc02b1d245d87e38f16d31a74df.
items.bottom_line: Local attackers can leverage a use-after-free flaw in the Linux kernel net scheduler packet classifier to escalate privileges to root.

items.title: CVE-2026-71513 (HIGH 8.7): NLTK before 3.10.3 contains a remote code execution vulnerability in AllowlistUnpickler that validates only t…
items.one_liner: NLTK < 3.10.3 allows remote code execution via unsafe attribute traversal in AllowlistUnpickler.
items.summary: NLTK before version 3.10.3 contains a remote code execution vulnerability in its AllowlistUnpickler implementation, which validates only the pickle module string rather than the global name. This oversight allows attackers to resolve dotted names via attribute traversal, reaching callables outside the intended allowlisted namespace. By crafting untrusted transition-parser models, attackers can trigger arbitrary command execution when TransitionParser.parse loads the model using allowlisted_pickle_load.
items.bottom_line: Attackers can achieve remote code execution in NLTK versions before 3.10.3 by supplying malicious transition-parser models that bypass pickling allowlists.

items.title: Granite 4.2 LLMs: How They're Built
items.one_liner: IBM's Granite 4.2 reasoning LLMs feature extended context windows, native tool calling, and an explicit thinking mode switch.
items.summary: IBM released Granite 4.2, a family of dense, decoder-only reasoning LLMs available in 3B, 8B, and 30B sizes under the Apache 2.0 license. Pre-trained from scratch on approximately 15 trillion tokens via a five-phase strategy, the models extend context windows up to 512K tokens and feature a multi-stage reinforcement learning pipeline. The 8B and 30B models include agentic RL to operate tools, execute code, and drive terminals in sandboxed environments. Every model includes a thinking / low-effort / non-thinking mode switch along with native OpenAI-compatible tool calling.
items.bottom_line: Granite 4.2 delivers open-weight reasoning models with native tool calling, configurable thinking budgets, and agentic RL training.

items.title: Agentic Security: A Systematization of Tools, Failure Modes, and Design Laws for LLM-Driven Penetration Testing
items.one_liner: This research provides a formal framework for understanding why your automated red-teaming agents might fail or exceed their intended scope.
items.summary: This research systematizes operational failures in agentic security systems that use LLMs to plan and execute penetration testing. Through an evaluation of ten common security tools, the authors identify recurring failure modes in unattended pipelines and introduce the Integration Friction Index to measure engineering and organizational costs. The study models these systems as stochastic policies within deterministic mediators, revealing that long-lived sessions often lose critical evidence over time. Crucially, the findings demonstrate that system prompts are insufficient for enforcing scope and budget, as they do not effectively constrain the actual execution of tools.
items.bottom_line: Scope and budget enforcement in agentic security cannot be delegated to system prompts because prompts do not reliably constrain what the system actually executes.

items.title: Beyond Over-Refusal: Defending Indirect Prompt Injection via Latent Instruction Manifolds
items.one_liner: AEGIS is a new adaptive ensemble guard designed to mitigate indirect prompt injection in LLM agents without incurring severe over-refusal.
items.summary: Indirect Prompt Injection attacks present major barriers to the safe deployment of LLMs integrated into complex ecosystems like code agents by exploiting the model's inability to distinguish instructions from data. Existing guardrails often fail by introducing high latency or severe over-refusal rates. To address this, researchers propose AEGIS (Adaptive Ensemble Guard for Injection Shielding), which extracts instruction-sensitive projectors and uses a Unified Multi-Layer Consensus mechanism across network depth. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that AEGIS achieves superior detection performance against heuristic and optimization-based attacks compared to baseline methods.
key_facts: Tool/Framework: AEGIS (Adaptive Ensemble Guard for Injection Shielding)
items.bottom_line: AEGIS separates instructions from data intrinsically via multi-layer consensus to defeat indirect prompt injections without over-refusal.

claims.text: AEGIS extracts instruction-sensitive projectors to identify malicious instructions and leverages a Unified Multi-Layer Consensus mechanism that aggregates topologically distinct signals across the network depth.

items.title: On Predicting Vulnerability Severity Using In-Context Learning: An Industrial Case Study
items.one_liner: Medium-sized open-source models like CodeLlama2-7B can locally predict vulnerability CVSS scores to provide privacy-preserving industrial triage.
items.summary: Modern software systems require scalable vulnerability severity assessment, but manual CVSS triage fails to scale with growing disclosures, while cloud LLM services present confidentiality concerns. Researchers conducted an industrial case study predicting CVSS v3.1 scores from vulnerable C/C++ code snippets using in-context learning with local, open-source LLMs. By comparing proprietary data against the Big-Vul dataset, the study evaluated models including CodeLlama2-7B, CodeLlama2-13B, Mistral-7B, gpt-oss, and GPT4o-mini. Results indicate that medium-sized models like CodeLlama2-7B can approximate cloud performance for CVSS regression when guided by output-constraining prompts.
key_facts: Models evaluated: CodeLlama2-7B, CodeLlama2-13B, Mistral-7B, gpt-oss, GPT4o-mini
items.bottom_line: Locally deployed open-source code models can effectively approximate cloud performance for automated CVSS severity prediction without data leakage.

claims.text: Our results show that medium-sized open-source code models, particularly CodeLlama2-7B, can approximate the best cloud performance for CVSS regression when guided by lightweight, output-constraining prompts, offering a practical, privacy-preserving building block for severity triage in industrial settings.
claims.support_span: Our results show that medium-sized open-source code models, particularly CodeLlama2-7B, can approximate the best cloud performance for CVSS regression when guided by lightweight, output-constraining prompts, offering a practical, privacy-preserving building block for severity triage in industrial settings.

items.title: SkillBloat: Token Amplification Attacks via Skill Injection in LLM Coding Agents
items.one_liner: A new 'denial-of-wallet' attack vector that exploits the very 'skills' you use to extend your coding agents.
items.summary: SkillBloat is a new token amplification attack targeting LLM coding agents through malicious "skill" injection. This economic resource-abuse threat causes agents to consume significantly more tokens than necessary, potentially leading to massive unexpected costs. The attack uses a two-phase framework: first screening for effective amplification mechanisms and then using an LLM to iteratively rewrite the skill for maximum impact. Testing on real-world benchmarks showed that SkillBloat can achieve up to 10x token amplification, proving that skill ecosystems are a viable surface for denial-of-wallet attacks.
items.bottom_line: Skill ecosystems in coding agents introduce a practical and effective surface for resource-exhaustion attacks that are distinct from traditional security vulnerabilities.

claims.text: SkillBloat achieved an average best token amplification of up to 10.1455x.

items.title: How Reliable Are NVD CWE Labels? A Large-Scale Semantic Audit with Seclometry
items.one_liner: A large-scale semantic audit of NVD CWE labels reveals that only half match code-grounded semantics, exposing structural metadata noise.
items.summary: CWE labels in the National Vulnerability Database serve as foundational ground truth for vulnerability search, scanning tools, and prioritization, yet their reliability has rarely been measured at scale. Researchers built CWEAgent, an auditing instrument based on 'seclometry' to evaluate CWE labeling quality across code semantics. When applied to 15,556 open-source CVEs from 2017 to 2026, the tool found that only 49.70% of NVD CWE labels precisely matched code-grounded labels, while 3.63% were evidence-inconsistent errors. The study highlights that CWE noise is a structural metadata issue rather than isolated annotation mistakes, with evidence-inconsistent labels increasing over time.
items.bottom_line: Security tools and scanners relying strictly on NVD CWE labels must account for widespread structural inaccuracy and metadata noise.

items.title: Towards Automated Cyber Threat Intelligence Elicitation in Underground Forums
items.one_liner: DarkBot is a multi-agent LLM system that actively elicits cyber threat intelligence from underground forums without detection or suspension.
items.summary: Gathering cyber threat intelligence from underground forums has become harder due to migration toward private spaces, rendering passive monitoring methods less effective. To counter this, researchers developed DarkBot, a multi-agent LLM-based system designed for active CTI elicitation in underground forums. The system organizes eleven specialized agents into blocks handling engagement gating, MITRE ATT&CK-driven context-aware question generation, and linguistic style adaptation. In evaluations across CrimeBB conversations and live forum deployments, the system successfully elicited CTI-relevant disclosures without triggering moderator interventions or account suspensions.
items.bottom_line: Active multi-agent systems can successfully extract cyber threat intelligence from hard-to-reach underground forums where passive monitoring fails.

items.title: Scalable PII Discovery in Mobile App Databases via Hypothesis-Driven Search
items.one_liner: A highly efficient tool for automating PII discovery in mobile forensics, directly relevant to DFIR and privacy auditing.
items.summary: This research presents a hypothesis-driven agentic framework for discovering personally identifiable information (PII) in complex mobile forensic databases. The system uses an agent to rank candidate table-column regions and probe sampled values, maintaining a memory of evidence to refine its search. This approach significantly reduces the need for exhaustive inspection of heterogeneous SQLite schemas. Testing on Android and iOS databases from the Cellebrite CTF corpus showed that Gemini 2.5 Pro could achieve a 94.5% F1 score while reducing the search space by nearly 80%.
items.bottom_line: Agentic, hypothesis-driven search can reduce the manual extraction search space in mobile forensic databases by 80% while maintaining high accuracy.

items.title: SecOPD: Mitigating Adaptive Prompt Injections by On-Policy Distillation
items.one_liner: SecOPD provides token-level feedback for defensive fine-tuning, dropping prompt injection attack success rates significantly on LLM agents.
items.summary: Prompt injection remains a major threat to AI agents interacting with external data sources like emails or files, and existing defensive fine-tuning methods often fail because they rely on coarse sequence-level feedback. To provide more granular supervision, researchers proposed Secure On-Policy Distillation (SecOPD), which supplies token-level feedback by scoring rollouts with an initialization model on clean inputs. Using this method, a defended Qwen3.6-27B model achieved a low 9.0% attack success rate against PISmith adaptive prompt injections compared to 94.0% for prior state-of-the-art Meta-SecAlign. Furthermore, the defense generalized effectively to unseen agentic tool-calling scenarios.
items.bottom_line: Token-level feedback via Secure On-Policy Distillation dramatically reduces prompt injection success rates compared to sequence-level tuning.

items.title: Closed-loop AI achieves certifiable engineering design
items.one_liner: The AI Engineer couples LLMs with deterministic physics solvers to achieve certified, optimized physical engineering designs.
items.summary: While agentic AI has advanced scientific discovery and coding, complex physical engineering design remains challenging because candidates must simultaneously satisfy multiple mechanical constraints. Researchers introduced The AI Engineer, an agentic framework coupling LLMs to deterministic engineering backends and solvers like CalculiX in a closed loop. An automated reviewer scores each design across five dimensions calibrated on 11 floating-wind projects, terminating search only when composite scores reach high thresholds. The certified engineering design successfully passed an external Approval in Principle from the China Classification Society, outperforming human baselines by reducing steel mass and unit capital cost by 8.1% each.
items.bottom_line: Closed-loop AI integration with deterministic physics solvers can successfully generate certifiable, cost-optimized physical engineering structures.

items.title: I Changed One “User_Id” and the API Said “Sure” — From Password Reset to Mass Account Takeover
items.one_liner: An API password-reset endpoint allowed unauthenticated mass account takeover simply by modifying the user ID parameter in the request body.
items.summary: During an authorized API penetration test, a researcher discovered a critical mass account takeover vulnerability within a password-reset endpoint. The backend API trusted client-supplied JSON parameters—specifically the User_Id field—without verifying authorization, session tokens, current passwords, or OTPs. By substituting the User_Id value, an attacker could silently change the password of any registered user on the platform. The flaw highlights the severe risks of client-side trust in sensitive authentication workflows.
items.bottom_line: Failing to validate server-side session authorization against user identifiers in password reset APIs allows full account compromise.

items.title: Caste divide makes summer more scorching in dry Indian region
items.one_liner: Severe heatwaves and water scarcity in Bundelkhand are intensifying caste discrimination and access barriers for Dalit families.
items.summary: In the drought-prone Bundelkhand region spanning Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, extreme summer temperatures exceeding 40°C have exacerbated severe water scarcity caused by dry government water schemes and dropping groundwater tables. Residents rely heavily on communal handpumps, leading to intense competition during early morning hours. For Dalits belonging to marginalized communities like the Valmikis, this scarcity intensifies entrenched caste discrimination, as they must wait until upper-caste residents finish using the pumps and frequently face ritualistic cleansing of the water sources afterward. While local officials and dominant-caste residents deny caste-based discrimination, Dalit families report ongoing social exclusion and fear of targeting amid the resource crunch.
key_facts: Region: Bundelkhand (Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh)
items.bottom_line: Climate-driven water scarcity in rural India is amplifying historical caste divides and friction at public water points.

items.title: India police clash with protesters a month after Gen Z demonstrations
